pairs.locus: William of Conches, Moralium Dogma Philosophorum, I.B.2.a (De beneficiis retribuendis)
pairs.question: Nam si Hesiodus iubet reddere maiore mensura que acceperis utenda, quid debemus facere prouocati beneficio?
pairs.answer: Imitari agros fertiles qui multo plus afferunt quam acceperunt.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question answered by the author himself. The conditional clause 'Nam si Hesiodus iubet reddere maiore mensura que acceperis utenda' is kept as verbatim setup so the question has its referent; the interrogative proper is 'quid debemus facere prouocati beneficio?'. The answer is the immediately following complete sentence to its first full stop; the text then opens a new rhetorical question ('Quia si non dubitamus officia conferre...'), which lies outside the answer window.

pairs.locus: William of Conches, Moralium Dogma Philosophorum, V (De conflictu honesti et utilis)
pairs.question: Nonne igitur sapiens, si fame ipse conficiatur, abstulerit cibum alteri homini ad nullam rem utili?
pairs.answer: Minime. Non enim est mihi uita utilior quam talis affectio animi, scilicet ut neminem uiolem causa mei commodi.
pairs.derivation: Objection-and-answer: the speech tag 'Forsitan quispiam dixerit:' is dropped as framing of the asking; the objection is a genuine interrogative ('Nonne... abstulerit cibum...?'), here normalized with a terminal '?'. The author answers in his own person; the answering speech tag 'inquam' is dropped as framing, leaving 'Minime.' as the operative reply, extended to its first full stop's worth of ground ('Non enim est mihi uita utilior... causa mei commodi.'). The window stops before the further elaboration ('Dum enim uita perditur...').
